issue.body:
As discussed in https://github.com/eslint/eslint/pull/7618, now that the indent rewrite has landed, we should enhance it with sane defaults for JSX, allowing for users who prefer to use a custom rule like [eslint-plugin-react](https://github.com/yannickcr/eslint-plugin-react) to do so with an `ignoreJSX` option.

__Note__: It already currently checks JSX. The proposal here is to update the rule to make it allow for common JSX styles and fix any bugs we see. Ideally, people won't have to use the `ignoreJSX` option. Actually, maybe we should hold off on that option and wait and see if anyone asks for it? It would be nice if everyone could just use the indent rule, since we support JSX out of the box!

So far, the following enhancements have been discussed:
- Allow for props to be inline or multiline indented one level
- Closing tags should be inline or indented at same level as opening tag
- The first level of indentation for JS expressions inside JSXExpressionContainer nodes needs to be calculated correctly

body: @not-an-aardvark I was thinking about implement a fix for this. Would we need a whitelist of known nodes that should be indented and all others be ignored?

Yes, I think that would probably be the best way to do it. Another option would be to use `espree.Syntax`, but that could cause breakage if new node types were added to espree in a minor release. For now, I suppose you could use `espree.Syntax` to get a one-time list of node types, and then hardcode that list into the file.

We would also have to make sure that indentation gets checked if a node is nested inside an ignored node. This is generally how ignored tokens work within the rule anyway, but we would need to accurately mark the right tokens as "ignored". The best way to do this might be to use `sourceCode.getNodeByRangeIndex` right before reporting a token for having incorrect indentation, and ignore the token if it's in an unknown node type. (Using `sourceCode.getNodeByRangeIndex` on every token in the file probably isn't feasible for performance reasons.)
